{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. flo2's proposal, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-21, in flo2's words: "Journal every write automatically — what changed, and who — instead of depending on the caller to call add_change_event."

HALF OF THIS IS ALREADY ACCEPTED INTENT AND UNBUILT. The WHO half was measured on 2026-08-10 and is a known hole: 0 of 360 ChangeEvents carried an author, and seat identity lived only on CLAIMS edges, which are advisory and released at checkout. That measurement named the exact fork this proposal walks into, and named it as the owner's to settle: whether attribution should be REQUIRED on a write, DEFAULTED FROM A SEAT, or left OPTIONAL — because required breaks every existing caller and optional makes it decorative. flo2 is effectively voting for "defaulted", and the identity it would default from is their other proposal.

🛑 THE OBJECTION THAT SHAPES THE ANSWER: A JOURNAL CANNOT KNOW WHY. This design already requires that a change record carry WHY in the same act that records it, and the reasoning is the whole value — 1063 ChangeEvents exist here and the standing complaint about them is not that there are too few. An automatic journal produces perfect what-and-who and no reason at all. If those rows enter the same ledger as the considered ones, the ledger gets bigger and thinner, and the next reader cannot tell a change somebody thought about from a row the server emitted.

⚠️ AND A BOUNDARY THAT MUST NOT BE CROSSED BY ACCIDENT. reflow2 already keeps a server-side ledger, and it is deliberately narrow: it records the VERB and never the OBJECT — which tool was called, never what it was called on — so that feedback carrying usage never carries the user's design content. That property has a CI gate behind it, proven to fail on an argument-leak mutation. An automatic write journal records objects BY DEFINITION. That is legitimate, because a change journal lives inside the user's own graph while telemetry leaves it — but the two records must stay separate and separately named, or the gate's guarantee erodes the first time somebody reuses the nearest existing mechanism.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A SEPARATE, THIN AUDIT TRAIL — the server appends what-and-who per write to its own log, NOT as ChangeEvents. `add_change_event` keeps its meaning: a considered record with a reason. Nothing gets thinner and the who-half question is answered. Costs a second record to read.
(b) AUTOMATIC ChangeEvents, marked as such — same rows, in the ledger, carrying a flag that says the server wrote this and nobody stated a reason. Queryable and honest, and it makes "which of our changes nobody explained" answerable for the first time. The risk is volume: writes here are frequent, the store does not branch with git, and this design has already caused phantom drift by writing on the wrong branch.
(c) THE WHO HALF ONLY — default an author onto ChangeEvents from the session's identity, and leave the caller responsible for creating them. The smallest change that closes the measured hole, and it needs the identity question settled first.
(d) DECLINE, and keep every change record deliberate.

WORTH NOTING: the same shape is already an open idea here — whether the server should count its own refusals so no session has to remember to. If the answer there is yes, the answer here probably follows, and both should be settled as one question about what the server records about itself rather than twice.

═══ ADDENDUM 2026-09-21, AFTER READING FLO2's OWN WRITE-UP (F31) RATHER THAN THE TWO-LINE RELAY ═══

🛑 THE "A JOURNAL CANNOT KNOW WHY" OBJECTION ABOVE IS NOT AN OBJECTION FLO2 MISSED. THEY RAISED IT THEMSELVES AND ANSWERED IT, and the answer is better than the way this node framed it. Their words, under a heading reading "The counter-argument, recorded rather than glossed": an automatic journal of every write gives a complete but noisy history, "a hundred mechanical entries where a person wants five meaningful ones", and no automatic journal will ever say why.

⭐ THEIR PROPOSAL IS THEREFORE **TWO TIERS, NOT A REPLACEMENT** — an automatic journal as the FLOOR that cannot be forgotten, and rich authored ChangeEvents on top for the changes that carry reasoning. That is option (a) or (b) above, not the wholesale substitution the relayed two-liner suggested.

⭐ AND THEIR TIEBREAK, WHICH THIS DESIGN SHOULD RECOGNISE AS ITS OWN PRINCIPLE ARRIVING FROM OUTSIDE: "If only one ships, the floor is the one that matters — a thin complete record beats a rich record with silent holes, because you can't tell a hole from an absence of change." That is cannot-tell-none-from-cannot-say. This project states it in `req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person` and has met it repeatedly; it is the argument that should carry the most weight here, and the version of this node written from the two-line relay gave it none.

THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THE ASK, which the relay did not carry: `fact:flo2-shipped-two-days-of-work-with-no-change-event-and-rebuilt-the-history-from-git-a-day-late`. Eight drifted artifacts with nothing in the design explaining them, found at a reconcile pass, reconstructed a day late from git log and memory. Their framing: "A history that depends on an agent remembering is exactly what git replaced — committing IS the act of recording, which is why git histories don't have holes."

WHY IT BLOCKS FLO2 SPECIFICALLY, which is the part that makes this a delivery question and not a modelling preference. Alex's accepted plan is ONE DESIGN, TWO DOORS: a non-technical person in a chat app, a developer in Claude Code / Codex / Grok Build. Without the journal, any write arriving through the developer's door is unrecorded — and the developer is the heaviest writer. So a returning collaborator asking "what changed while I was away?" gets a confident answer missing exactly the changes that mattered most. With it, flo2's open question about which tool surface a developer should get drops from a data-integrity problem to an ordinary product question, answerable either way.

📌 FLO2 CALLS THIS "the biggest ask in this document", and characterises it as COMPLETION RATHER THAN INVENTION: `mint_seat`, `add_contributor`, `authored_by`, `claim_region` and the whole ChangeEvent/Snapshot/DesignEpoch model are already built. What is missing is that every piece is opt-in, "so the record is only as good as the caller's memory — and the caller is an LLM with 181 tools and a long task."
